owner: CC gates writes to cairn/devices/inference_domain/ (its charter's gated_by). No spec question stands at Akien's gate here: whether the meter should account for a refusal at all is settled by the charter's own how_it_learns, not by a ruling.
intention: yield_report names its refusals, so a reader of the meter can tell a call that was answered from one that was refused instead of being handed three numbers that no longer add up.
why: The lived symptom is on a surface Akien reads. cairn/devices/librarian/live.py prints the whole yield dict at four sites and cairn/devices/intention_extractor/live.py at one more; since 2026-08-18 the printed numbers do not sum — calls 2564 against hits 1152 + misses 1411 = 2563 — and nothing on the surface says why. The missing row is the first refusal this system ever recorded. A diagnostic surface that quietly folds a third outcome into a total is Law 7's collapse happening at the exact place the system reports its own honesty about inference spend.
how: Add a `refused` count beside `hits` and `misses` (rows with verdict='refused'), leaving `calls`, `hits`, `misses`, `spent` and `avoided` meaning exactly what they mean today. That turns calls == hits + misses + refused into a checkable identity rather than a broken one, and it is the smallest change that moves no meaning under a standing reader. A tooth asserts the identity over a corpus holding a refused row written by the REAL writer, not a hand-built fixture.
traces_to: Law 7 — errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth. yield_report is a diagnostic surface with six live human-facing print sites, and it currently collapses a refusal into a total.
Law 3 — the meter is what makes the saving a measured fact; a meter whose parts do not sum is one a reader has to distrust.
Telos 1 (T1.2 — every call metered because this is the sole pipe)
gates: Proof gate: cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_domain.py, run by the tester and sealed under netns — the same proof that already owns the meter's teeth, because the meter is what changes. Check-type: deterministic code tooth (an arithmetic identity over rows read back through store.read, plus a real refused row written through domain.resolve rather than hand-built). Feedback-to-origin on failure: the WATCHME probe below re-opens at the owner's gate (Law 6) — the probe deposits and pokes, it decides nothing. Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed. Owner: CC (cairn/devices/inference_domain/intention+why.json, gated_by).
falsifier: FALSIFIER: DONE when yield_report returns a `refused` count and calls == hits + misses + refused holds as a proof tooth over a corpus containing at least one refused row written by the real writer. RED on any of: (1) a reader can still compute hits + misses and silently miss refusals; (2) spent or avoided move — a refusal costs nothing and must enter neither; (3) the identity is asserted only over hand-built fixture rows and never over a row the producer made. HORIZON: the next verdict value added to inference_calls. It should RED this tooth rather than pass it — an identity that survives a fourth value is an identity that stopped checking anything.
horizon: The next verdict value added to inference_calls. It should RED this tooth rather than pass it — an identity that survives a fourth value is an identity that stopped checking anything.
children: none, because the whole change is one dict key and one tooth at one address (cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py, yield_report at line 302) plus its probe; a decomposition here would be ceremony over a single seam. The larger question it touches — that the verdict vocabulary is enforced by no CHECK constraint because db_domain has no migration primitive — is a SIBLING cast, not a child of this one, and is being cast in the same sitting.
dependencies: a-refused-ask-leaves-a-row (PROVED 2026-08-18) — the refused row this meter must account for

watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: the distinct verdict values found past the era, the count of rows at each, the set yield_report accounts for, and the arithmetic difference between calls and the accounted sum (zero is the passing value).
watchme.consumer: whoever next reads the librarian's or the extractor's live output and needs the numbers to add up — and the next builder to add a verdict value, who should find this red rather than discover the under-count in a print months later.
watchme.enough: enough when the store has carried all three accounted verdicts past the era (at least one 'hit', one 'miss' and one 'refused') with the identity calls == hits + misses + refused holding on every read, and no unaccounted verdict value has appeared. The first half proves the accounting is exercised rather than merely written; the second is the standing question, which is why this watch is not a restatement of the build tooth — the tooth reads a corpus the build made, the probe reads the vocabulary the world produces.
watchme.trigger: each read of inference_calls — the probe collects the DISTINCT verdict values actually present in the store past its era and compares them against the set yield_report accounts for. It rides traffic that already exists and needs no clock and no host.

from_idea: none, because it was born inside a build rather than captured. The owed ticket is named in three places already on disk: the cast ticket a-refused-ask-leaves-a-row , the charter at cairn/devices/inference_domain/intention+why.json (falsifier clause 10, residue), and cairn commit ad5a601's message.
provenance: Born as the honest residue of a-refused-ask-leaves-a-row. That voyage taught the domain to record a refused ask; `calls` in yield_report is len(rows), so it began counting refusals the same hour and stopped equalling hits + misses. constrain's bounds.in for that voyage named resolve() and NOT the meter, so fixing it there would have been a bounds change without the word — a silent widening. The rule asked for a ticket instead; this is it, cast the same night, with the discrepancy measured live rather than predicted.
standing_note: STANDING IN QUESTION AS OF 2026-08-18, same reason as its sibling the-verdict-vocabulary-is-held-by-postgres: Akien has stated the design this row shape sits inside — an inference call creates a task ticket carrying the whole call, with a trouble raised on failure pointing at the log entry and an intelligible message back when nothing can resolve it. Verbatim at CairnCommons/ideas/2026-08-18-intention-an-infernce-call-is-made-a.json. A 'refused' counter on yield_report may survive that reshape or may be answering the wrong question. DO NOT BUILD UNTIL THE RESHAPE IS SETTLED. The measured defect it names is real either way: yield_report's `calls` is len(rows) and since the refusal write it no longer equals hits + misses (2564 vs 2563 at the close), on a surface librarian and intention_extractor print to a human.
